judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of al-Sharaṭān, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (alif). When the moon descends into al-Sharaṭān — and it is fiery and inauspicious — there are valid in it such operations as pertain to the affairs of women. A spiritual force is stirred toward that, joined to the souls of kings; and in it there appear among them anger, violent seizure, and the shedding of blood. In this period the sages used to settle to sleep and to the absence of movement. Some of them have mentioned that a man sees in his sleep what strikes at him and troubles his temper, and that not sleeping at this time is preferable; and that one must hold to silence, speaking only of what is necessary or of what cannot be avoided.

stars.t: I say, concerning the figures of the mansions — and we have already made them plain in a manner other than this first one — that the first of them is al-Sharaṭayn: two stars set apart, one of them on the southern side and the other on the northern side, and they are the two horns of Aries; the brighter of the two is called al-Nāṭiḥ. To the eye's estimation, when they stand at mid-heaven the distance between them is about ten cubits. Near al-Simāk is a small star that sometimes goes before them. And this is the figure of al-Sharaṭayn: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ]

mansions.rising: The rising of al-Sharaṭayn falls when 19 nights of Nīsān (April) have elapsed, and on that day the Sun lodges in al-Iklīl.

judge.t: The discourse on al-Buṭayn, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (bāʾ). When the moon descends into al-Buṭayn — and it is hot and moist — there descends into the world /fol. 15r./ a wholesome, temperate spiritual force, fit for what pertains to the affairs of men rather than of women. In it talismans are set up; the operation of alchemy is valid in it, and every craft of exalted degree; and there are fit in it the commencement of the sciences, the casting of signet-rings, and engraving. Whoever is born in it lives happy, rightly guided, and beloved of created beings. Its suffumigation is aloeswood, saffron, and mastic.

stars.t: As for al-Buṭayn, it is three small, dim stars forming an equilateral triangle, and they are the belly of Aries (al-Ḥamal). It was given a diminutive form only because Aries is many stars in the shape of a ram: al-Buṭayn is its belly, al-Thurayyā its fat tail, and al-Sharaṭayn its two horns. And the figure of al-Buṭayn is thus: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ]

mansions.rising: The rising of al-Buṭayn falls when one night of it remains.

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of al-Thurayyā, and this is its figure, and it is as you see: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (jīm). When the moon descends into al-Thurayyā — and it is a star of mixed substance — there descends into the world a spiritual force of mixed heat and cold. The making of talismans is fit in it; do in it what is fit for women, and the preparation of medicines efficacious against cold. Travellers fare well in it and gain abundant profit; and it is good in it to meet kings and to correspond with them. In it marriage is fit, and the purchase of slave-girls and of slaves; and whatever is undertaken in it is good, because it is the counterpart of the moon and not of the sun; and whatever is made in it is of praiseworthy outcome. Whoever is born in it will be fortunate: he detests debauchery, loves piety, and consorts with the righteous and the learned. Its suffumigation is linseed and black cumin. And God knows best.

stars.t: As for al-Thurayyā (the Pleiades), it is seven stars, six of them visible and one small and hidden, by which people test their eyesight. It was called /fol. 18v./ al-Thurayyā only from al-tharwa, which is abundance of dew and moisture. It has [several] names, among them al-Najm (the Star), even though in number they are stars. Some of the learned have said that what is intended by His words, exalted is He, By the star when it falls (Q 53:1) is al-Thurayyā, according to one of the opinions, and that the Arabs call al-Thurayyā a single "star" even though they are stars in number. The Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — likewise called it "the Star", for he said, upon him be blessing and peace: ((When the Star rises, blight is lifted)) — meaning al-Thurayyā; and he meant [the lifting of blight] from the fruits. Among its names, too, are al-ʿUnqūd (the Cluster) and al-Qadam (the Foot) — so understand. And someone has recited these two verses:

mansions.rising: The rising of al-Thurayyā falls on the 13th of Ayyār (May); and it travels on for 50 nights after it has set at the west, then appears at daybreak from the east. When it stands at mid-heaven together with the setting of the sun, the cold grows severe and the blights are lifted from the fruits. And we have related that the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((When the Star rises, the blights are lifted.))

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of al-Dabarān, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (dāl). When the moon descends into al-Dabarān — and it is earthy — there descends into the world a spiritual force that works enmity, hatred, and corruption in the earth. So beware in it of striving after your needs and of beginning operations. Set up no talisman in it, and undertake no craft in it. In sum, all operations in it are of evil outcome. It is fit for nothing save the burying of the dead, the hoarding of wealth, the concealing of secrets, the digging of wells, and the cutting of river channels; it is fit for nothing besides that. Whoever is born in it will be blameworthy and forsaken. Its suffumigation is the rind of sweet pomegranate and male frankincense. And God knows best.

stars.t: As for al-Dabarān, it is the fat tail of Aries. It was so named — so it is said — because it comes behind (istadbara) al-Thurayyā. Some have said that it is five stars in Taurus (al-Thawr), and it is said of them that they are ill-omened. Its figure is thus: [Figure: star-diagram as in source

mansions.rising: The rising of al-Dabarān falls on the 26th of Ayyār.

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of al-Haqʿa, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (hāʾ). When the moon descends into al-Haqʿa — and it is mixed of inauspicious and auspicious — there descends into the earth a spiritual force that is at one time evil and at another mixed. So work in it at the violent workings of poisons and their compounds in particular. Undertake in it no craft of the sun and the moon; plant no crop in it; wear no garments in it, neither new nor worn; and do not marry in it, for all of that is of unpraiseworthy outcome. Stir not in it with anything of the operations of the spiritual beings. Whoever is born in it will be of praiseworthy outcome at the end of his life, but not at its beginning. Its suffumigation for that is nadd aloeswood, frankincense, benzoin (jāwī), and mastic.

stars.t: As for al-Haqʿa, it is three bright stars close to one another, and it is the head of al-Jawzāʾ (Orion), as though they were three fingers held together. Its figure is thus: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ] And it is said that it is the whorl that lies on the flank of a beast, at the rider's foot. Ibn ʿAbbās — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — was asked about a man who divorced his wife by the number of the stars of heaven, and he said: "The Haqʿa of al-Jawzāʾ suffices him." And it is a mighty light.

mansions.rising: The rising of al-Haqʿa falls when eight [nights] of Ḥazīrān (June) have elapsed.

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of al-Hanʿa, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (wāw). When the moon descends into al-Hanʿa — and it is an auspicious star — then work in it the operations of inclining, /fol. 15v./ love, and affection; suffumigate in it with the incense; go in, in it, to kings and to the great ones; strive after their needs, and strive about their quarter; and in it join yourself to the noble among people and consort with the brethren. Begin in it the operations you desire; marry in it; buy in it slave-girls, slaves, and horses; plant trees in it; raise buildings in it; measure and weigh; travel in it; and sell and buy — all of that is of praiseworthy outcome. Whoever is born in it lives happy and dies a martyr. Its suffumigation is quṭrub and wormwood seed.

stars.t: As for al-Hanʿa, it is the left shoulder of al-Jawzāʾ, and it is five stars ranged in a row. And it is said that it is two large stars with three small ones between them; but what is apparent is that they are five. Its figure is thus: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ] It was called al-Hanʿa only because each one of them bends toward its companion; one says hanaʿtu al-shayʾ, that is, "I bent it".

mansions.rising: The rising of al-Hanʿa falls on the 21st of it.

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of al-Dhirāʿ, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (zāy). When the moon descends into al-Dhirāʿ — and it is airy, auspicious, and gentle — there descends into the world a wholesome spiritual force, fit for the handling of the spiritual beings, for the beginning of good works, for the suffumigations, and for assembling in houses of worship. In it talismans are set up, and in it are performed the operations of the nāranjiyyāt (nīranj-workings). In it one goes in to kings, and joins oneself to the noble among people and to the brethren. Whoever is born in it will be fortunate, rightly guided, and granted success. Its suffumigation is nettle seed and linseed.

stars.t: As for al-Dhirāʿ, it is said that it is the foreleg of Leo (al-Asad), and it is two bright stars. And it is said that they are two stars with small stars between them /fol. 19r./ called al-Aẓfār (the Claws), as though they were the talons of the lion; and between the two, to the eye, is the measure of a course (shawṭ). They are two forelegs, one of them outstretched and the other drawn in, which is not in line with the [first] foreleg, and the other is as though contracted away from it; and the outstretched one is higher in the sky. The bright one of the two is called al-Shiʿrā al-Ghumayṣāʾ (Procyon), because when she proved unable to cross the Milky Way and overtake her companion — who is al-Shiʿrā al-ʿAbūr (Sirius) — she wept until her eye grew dim. And it is said that she wept because she could not overtake Suhayl (Canopus).

mansions.rising: The rising of al-Dhirāʿ falls when four [nights] of Tammūz (July) have elapsed.

judge.t: The discourse on al-Nathra, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (ḥāʾ). When the moon descends into al-Nathra — and it is cold mixed with heat, auspicious mixed with inauspicious — there descends into the world a spiritual force that works upon enmity, hatred, the severing of ties, and the like. It is fit for the making of the talismans that serve for that, and for invoking wrath upon enemies, transgressors, and the rancorous. In it the spiritual force of anger is stirred. So undertake in it no craft of the sun and the moon; do not go in to kings in it; and do not begin the making of the instruments of war, nor take counsel concerning them, for it is evil, and fit [only] for the operations of corruption, as we have mentioned. Whoever is born in it will be ill-starred. Its suffumigation is costus and pomegranate rind.

stars.t: As for al-Nathra, it is two stars with the measure of a span between them, and in it is a smudge of whiteness like a scrap of cloud; and it is the nose of the lion. And it is said that it is three stars. Its figure is thus: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ] It lies between the lion's mouth and his nostrils, and it is called Makhṭat al-Asad (the lion's nasal discharge).

mansions.rising: The rising of al-Nathra falls when 17 nights of it have elapsed, together with the rising of al-Shiʿrā al-ʿAbūr.

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of al-Ṭarf, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (ṭāʾ). When the moon descends into al-Ṭarf — and it is a watery star, continuously inauspicious — there descends into the world a spiritual force that indicates the like of what has gone before, and its action is the stronger. So set up no talisman in it; undertake no craft in it; do not go in to kings in it; begin nothing of affection in it; and work no work of wisdom in it. Recite no adjuration. Solitude in it is better than mingling; and it is evil for all operations. Whoever is born in it will be ill-starred. Its suffumigation is nadd aloeswood and saffron.

stars.t: As for al-Ṭarf, it is two stars that go before al-Jabha, and they are the two eyes of the lion. And it is said that between them is the measure of a man's height (qāma). Their figure is thus: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ]

mansions.rising: The rising of al-Ṭarf falls on the first night of Āb (August).

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of al-Jabha, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs (yāʾ). When the moon descends into al-Jabha — and it is cold, auspicious, mixed with inauspicious, and it is nearer to good than to corruption — in it one begins works of affection, and operations whose means lie near at hand, and going in to kings, and asking for what may be obtained through the fulfilment of needs. In it one is treated, and in it are treated slight ailments that are easily cured /fol. 16r./. In it removal from place to place, and travel, are fit; but the cutting out of new clothing and the wearing of it is disliked in it. Whoever is born in it will be adroit, fortunate, and granted success, though there is in him some guile and deceit. Its suffumigation is myrtle berries and saffron.

stars.t: As for al-Jabha, it is the forehead of the lion, and it is four stars, one of them glittering, which is the southern one (al-Yamānī); between every two stars, to the eye, is the measure of a course. It is called Nawʾ al-Asad (the lion's rain-star), and it follows upon al-Ṭarf. Its figure is thus: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ]

mansions.rising: The rising of al-Jabha falls when 14 nights of it have elapsed.

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of al-Kharthān, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (kāf). When the moon descends into al-Kharthān — and it is al-Zubra — and it is hot and dry, it is fit for the handling of the spiritual beings, and for setting up talismans in it, and for the treatment of the sick and the curing of the chronically disabled, and for selling and buying, and for going in to kings and to chiefs. In it is fit the journey whose establishment one aims at, and residence; in it operations of exalted degree are fit; and in it the wearing of new clothing is fit. Whoever is born in it will be beloved among people, save that there is in him some guile, deceit, and dissimulation. Its suffumigation is the rind of sweet pomegranate, and nothing else. And God knows best.

stars.t: As for al-Zubra, it is two stars, and they are the two withers of the lion, the place of the mane upon his shoulders; and between them, to the eye, is the measure of a course. Their figure is thus: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ]

mansions.rising: The rising of al-Zubra falls on the 29th of it.

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of al-Ṣarfa, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs (lām). When the moon descends into al-Ṣarfa — and it is a star of mixed substance, of earth and fire — there descends into the world an auspicious spiritual force, fit for such operations as are middling. No craft is undertaken in it; the sick are not treated in it; and one does not go in to kings. But in it the instruments of war are made, in it arms are borne, and horses ridden. Whoever is born in it will be of evil disposition; he shuns people and people shun him — a schemer, a trickster, wicked, whom no one loves, by reason of the greatness of his evil and his guile. And God, exalted is He, knows best. Its suffumigation is nutmeg.

stars.t: As for al-Ṣarfa, it is a single bright star facing al-Zubra. And it is said that it is the heart of the lion. It was called Ṣarfa only because with it the cold turns away (inṣirāf) and the heat comes on; and it is said that at its rising the heat turns away. Its figure is thus: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ]

mansions.rising: The rising of al-Ṣarfa falls when 8 [nights] of Aylūl (September) have elapsed.

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of al-ʿAwwāʾ, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (mīm). When the moon descends into al-ʿAwwāʾ — and it is a hot, dry star, auspicious mixed with inauspicious — there descends into the world a spiritual force that stirs up desire and engenders in men love for women and union with them. It is fit for the beginning of the teaching of knowledge and the teaching of everything. Do not undertake in it the craft of the noble stone, for it does not suit it. Do not make war upon enemies in it; let there be no quarrelling and no litigating; and do not go in to kings. It is fit that you wear new garments in it, and that garments be cut out in it. Whoever is born in it, male or female, will be a possessor of good fortune. The suffumigation for that is male frankincense. And God knows best.

stars.t: As for al-ʿAwwāʾ, it is five stars, said to be the haunch of the lion. And its figure: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ]

mansions.rising: The rising of al-ʿAwwāʾ falls when 19 nights of it have elapsed.

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of al-Simāk, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (nūn). When the moon descends into al-Simāk — and it is an earthy, dry star — there descends into the world a spiritual force that engenders enmity and the corruption of woman. It is fit for the making of deadly poisons and everything that engenders corruption. Beginning new and beneficial works is disliked, and selling, buying, and barter are disliked in it. Whoever is born in it will be a talebearer and a liar, of unpraiseworthy outcome. Its suffumigation is male frankincense and indigo seed.

stars.t: As for al-Simāk, it is two bright stars: al-Simāk al-Aʿzal (Spica), which is one of the lunar mansions, and al-Simāk al-Rāmiḥ (Arcturus), which is not one of the lunar mansions. They are two stars. And it is said that they are the foot of the lion; and it is said that one of the two is one of the lion's shanks and the other is the other shank. With al-Rāmiḥthere is another star before it, which is its lance (rumḥ); while al-Aʿzal stands apart from the stars, no star coming near it. It was called al-Aʿzal ("the unarmed") because it has no lance, and it was called Simāk because it samaka in the sky, that is, it rose high. The figure of al-Aʿzal is thus: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ] And the figure of al-Rāmiḥis thus: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ] Behind al-Rāmiḥis a star called al-Fakka — and it is said al-Falaka — which is a circular constellation, and it is called Qaṣʿat al-Masākīn (the beggars' bowl); but in fact al-Fakka lies before al-Rāmiḥ. And ʿArsh al-Simāk (the throne of al-Simāk) is four small stars below al-ʿAwwāʾ, called ʿAjuz al-Asad (the lion's rump). As for al-Simāk al-Aʿzal, it is the boundary between the southern (Yamānī) and the northern (Shāmī) stars.

mansions.rising: The rising of [al-Simāk] falls when 2 nights of it remain.

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of al-Ghafr, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source] [editor's gloss (Old Spanish, fragmentary, standing in the figure area together with the numeral= 2): "…oble en ella quier cosa" — "…‑oble; in it, any thing"]. To it belongs the letter (sīn). When the moon descends into al-Ghafr — and it is an airy star there descends /fol. 16v./ during it into the world a spiritual force (rūḥāniyya) that produces love, affection, repose, and profit from kings. During it medicines are gathered, and those substances by which lethal poisons are dissolved and their harm repelled. During it the conducting of [the operation of] the noble stone is favourable; during it one works upon the spiritual beings; during it talismans are set up; and one may practise whatever accords with that among all the crafts and trades. Whoever is born under it will be ill-starred, possessed of cunning and deceit. And God knows best. Its suffumigation is male frankincense, and nothing else.

stars.t: As for al-Ghafr, it is three /fol. 19v./ small stars in which the Moon lodges, and they belong to Libra (al-Mīzān). And it is said that it is taken from al-ghafra, which is the tuft of hair at the tip of the lion's tail. Its figure is thus: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ]

mansions.rising: The rising of [al-Ghafr] falls on the 12th of Tishrīn al-Awwal (October).

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of al-Zubānā, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (ʿayn). When the moon descends into al-Zubānā — it is an airy star, auspicious but mixed with inauspiciousness — there descends during it into the world a spiritual force of a thing and its opposite; so operate during it in accordance with that. Whoever puts on a new garment [during it], a dog's bite will befall him, and enemies will speak evil words against him, and an ailment will fasten upon his body that pains him, and he will be hard put to be cured of it. Whoever is born under it will be fortunate in all his movements, whether male or female, though there is in him some cunning. And God knows best. Its suffumigation is wormwood seed and wild chamomile.

stars.t: As for al-Zubānā, it is the two claws of Scorpio (al-ʿAqrab), and they are two bright stars. And its description is thus: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ]

mansions.rising: The rising of [al-Zubānā] falls on the 25th of it.

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of al-Iklīl, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (fāʾ). When the moon descends into al-Iklīl — it is a star mixed of auspicious and inauspicious — there descends during it into the world a spiritual force that engenders enmity, hatred, and strife, and it works during it a thing and its opposite. Do not travel during it, do not marry, do not buy slaves, do not plant fruit-bearing trees or any others, and do not sow any crop: all of that is of unpraiseworthy outcome. Do not make up new garments during it, nor wear them; do not quarrel during it, nor go to law; and do not seek during it the fulfilment of needs. Whoever is born under it, whether male or female, will turn out base and ill-omened. Its suffumigation is pepper, saffron, and aloeswood.

stars.t: As for al-Iklīl, it is four stars ranged in a row, and this is its figure: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ] And it is said that they are three, the head of the scorpion, as though it were the crown (iklīl) upon the head.

mansions.rising: The rising of [al-Iklīl] falls on the 8th of Tishrīn al-Thānī (November).

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of al-Qalb, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (ṣād). When the moon descends into al-Qalb — it is a fortunate star, watery and moist — there descends during it into the world a spiritual force that sets right what the preceding mansion has corrupted. It is favourable for buying weapons and the instruments of war, and for buying riding-beasts, and for farriery, and for uprooting trees, and for sowing and ploughing, and for bringing out what lies buried, and for treating livestock, and for drinking purgative medicines, and for bloodletting and cupping. Whoever is born under it will be ill-starred, whether male or female, though there is in him some cunning. And God knows best. Its suffumigation is myrobalan leaves.

stars.t: As for al-Qalb, it is the heart of the scorpion, and it is a bright star with two stars at its side. And this is their figure: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ]

mansions.rising: The rising of [al-Qalb] falls on the 21st of it.

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of al-Shawla, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (qāf). When the moon descends into al-Shawla — it is an auspicious star turned aside by inauspiciousness — there descends during it into the world a mixed spiritual force that works during it a thing and its opposite. It is favourable for binding and loosing, and for such operations as are middling. But during it the cutting out of new clothing and the wearing of it are disapproved; do not set up a talisman during it, nor work upon the spiritual beings during it. Withdrawal from company during it is of praiseworthy outcome. Whoever is born under it, whether male or female, will be base, ill-omened, an inveterate liar, a talebearer, and depraved. Its suffumigation is pomegranate rind and mastic.

stars.t: As for al-Shawla, it is two stars close together, called Ḥumat al-ʿAqrab (the scorpion's sting). And this is their description: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ] Some have said that it is the tail of the scorpion, taken from al-shawl, which is "raising up", as though it were sāʾila, that is, uplifted and advancing. And some have said that it lies outside the Milky Way.

mansions.rising: The rising of [al-Shawla] falls when 3 [nights] of Kānūn al-Awwal (December) have elapsed.

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of al-Naʿāʾim, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (rāʾ). When the moon descends into al-Naʿāʾim, /fol. 17r./ it being fiery, fortunate, luminous, shining, and radiant, there descends during it into the world a spiritual force that purifies hearts and summons to affection, good fortune, and felicity; and it is of praiseworthy outcome in all circumstances. During it the conducting of the noble crafts is favourable; during it sayings of wisdom and the sciences of jurisprudence are recited; during it talismans are set up; during it building is built; and plant plantings during it, and wear new clothing during it, and cut out new clothing as well — for whoever wears new clothing will not cease to be in joy and gladness until that garment wears out. Whoever is born under it, whether male or female, will be granted success in all his movements and his restings. Its suffumigation is male frankincense and wormwood, and God knows best.

stars.t: [ As for al-Naʿāʾim … ] — as though they had drunk and then turned away. And it is said that they resemble the timbers that are hung over the mouth of a well, upon which the pulley and the ropes are hung; and they are called al-Naʿāʾim.

mansions.rising: The rising of [al-Naʿāʾim] falls when 16 nights of it have elapsed.

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of al-Balda, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (shīn). When the moon descends into al-Balda — it is a fiery, inauspicious star — there descends during it into the world a spiritual force that works upon enmity, hatred, the severing of ties, and every evil; and nothing but that is to be done during it. So beware of setting up a talisman during it; do not conduct during it the operation of the noble stone or of the magnified gem; do not work upon the spiritual beings during it; do not sow any crop during it, nor set any planting; do not undertake any journey during it; and do not consort with kings during it. Whoever is born under it, whether male or female, will be ill-omened and a schemer. Its suffumigation is spikenard, aloeswood, and nadd, and God knows best.

stars.t: As for al-Balda, it is six stars belonging to Sagittarius (al-Qaws), in which the Sun lodges on the shortest day of the year. Some have said that al-Balda is the gap between the two eyebrows. Its figure is thus: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ]

mansions.rising: The rising of [al-Balda] falls when 29 nights of it have elapsed.

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of Saʿd al-Dhābiḥ, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (tāʾ). When the moon descends into Saʿd al-Dhābiḥ— it is an earthy star, inauspicious and mixed — there descends during it into the world a spiritual force that works during it hatred, enmity, and the severing of ties. The outcomes of affairs and of operations are not praiseworthy during it; during it the souls of kings are stirred to anger and wrath; and buying and selling are held blameworthy during it. Whoever is born under it, whether male or female, will be blessed, avid for this world, and a schemer after it. Its suffumigation is safflower.

stars.t: As for Saʿd al-Dhābiḥ, it is two bright stars with the measure of a cubit between them; and close by each of the two is a small star near it, as though it were slaughtering it, and it was for that reason called al-Dhābiḥ (the Slaughterer). And this is its figure: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ]

mansions.rising: The rising of Saʿd al-Dhābiḥfalls when 11 nights of Kānūn al-Thānī (January) have elapsed. [

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of Saʿd Bulaʿ, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (thāʾ). When the moon descends into Saʿd Bulaʿ — it is a star mixed in substance, auspicious mixed with inauspicious — there descends during it into the world a spiritual force that works a thing and its opposite; it stands between the good and the bad. During it the buying of slaves and bondsmen is favourable, and it is suitable for buying riding-beasts, and for consorting with elders advanced in years, and for undertaking agricultural labours, and for cutting canals and digging wells, and for whatever of such works one may wish. It is suitable for excursions and outings, and for preparing foods and banquet-spreads. Whoever is born under it, whether male or female, will be blessed and righteous. Its suffumigation is chamomile.

stars.t: As for Saʿd Bulaʿ, it too is a single star, as though it were an open mouth wishing to swallow something. And this is its figure: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ]

mansions.rising: The rising of Saʿd Bulaʿ] falls when 24 [nights] of it have elapsed.

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of Saʿd al-Suʿūd, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (khāʾ). When the moon descends into Saʿd al-Suʿūd — it is a star mixed in substance, of earth and of air — there descends during it into the world /fol. 17v./ a spiritual force that effaces the traces of what came before it and is favourable for all operations. So begin during it with the operation of love and affection, and with whatever you wish of the acts that pertain to the mending of hearts. Work upon the spiritual beings during it, and set up talismans during it, and make contact during it with kings, chiefs, holders of office, and others; and do during it whatever you wish of the acts of affection — your operation will succeed. Whoever is born under it, whether male or female, will love the righteous. Its suffumigation is aloeswood and mastic, and God knows best.

stars.t: As for Saʿd al-Suʿūd, it is a single bright, solitary star which brings down felicity. And this is its figure: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ]

mansions.rising: The rising of Saʿd [al-Suʿūd] /fol. 20v./ falls when 6 [nights] of Shubāṭ (February) have elapsed.

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of Saʿd al-Akhbiya, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (dhāl). When the moon descends into Saʿd al-Akhbiya — it is an airy, inauspicious star — there descends during it into the world a spiritual force that works during it the severing of ties, seditions, hatred, division, and wars. Operations are not brought to completion, and if they are completed their outcome is not praiseworthy. Do not treat the sick during it, nor undertake the treatments of spirits and of spiritual beings; do not set up talismans during it; and do not conduct during it the operation of alchemy (kīmiyāʾ) or of sīmiyāʾ. Whoever is born under it, whether male or female, will be depraved and an arrant unbeliever. Its suffumigation is male frankincense, sarcocolla (ʿanzarūt), and pepper.

stars.t: As for Saʿd al-Akhbiya, it is three stars like the three hearth-stones (athāfī), with a fourth star beneath one of them. And this is its figure: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ] And it is said that they are two stars. Some of them have said that the first of the Saʿds is Saʿd al-Suʿūd, then Saʿd al-Dhābiḥ, then Saʿd al-Akhbiya, then Saʿd Bulaʿ. The Saʿd stars are ten, four of them in the sign of Capricorn (al-Jady), in which the Moon lodges — and the four have been mentioned. As for the six that are not among the lunar mansions, they are Saʿd Nāshira, Saʿd al-Malik, Saʿd al-Bihām, Saʿd al-Humām, Saʿd al-Bāriʿ, and Saʿd Maṭar. Each Saʿd of these six has two stars, and between every two stars of them, to the eye, is the measure of a cubit; and they are ranged in sequence.

mansions.rising: The rising of Saʿd [al-Akhbiya] falls when 18 [nights] of it have elapsed.

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of al-Fargh al-Muqaddam, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (ḍād). When the moon descends into al-Fargh al-Muqaddam — it is a watery, fortunate star — there descends during it into the world a spiritual force that works love during it, stirs up desire during it, and quickens souls with affection. During it the conducting of the alchemical operation is favourable, and the treatments of the spiritual beings, and the setting up of talismans, and the science of sīmiyāʾ. During it beneficial medicines are gathered; during it one may go in before kings and chiefs; and during it poisons are dissolved. Whoever is born under it will be of praiseworthy outcome. Its suffumigation is male frankincense, black cumin, and saffron. And God knows best, and that suffices.

stars.t: As for al-Fargh of the Bucket, the fore and the hind: each of the two is two stars, and between each star of them and the other are five cubits, as though the two were emptying out of the buckets. Al-Fargh al-Muʾakhkhar is the outlet of the water from the bucket, between the ʿarāqī (the cross-bars). And it is said that they are called al-Farghānī.

mansions.rising: The rising of al-Fargh al-Muqaddam (the fore Fargh) falls when 2 nights of Ādhār (March) have elapsed.

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of al-Fargh al-Muʾakhkhar, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (ẓāʾ). When the moon descends into al-Fargh al-Muʾakhkhar — it is a watery, fortunate star — there descends during it into the world a spiritual force that governs during it operations whose outcome is not praiseworthy, as was said above concerning the inauspicious mansions.

stars.t: As for al-Fargh of the Bucket, the fore and the hind: each of the two is two stars, and between each star of them and the other are five cubits, as though the two were emptying out of the buckets. Al-Fargh al-Muʾakhkhar is the outlet of the water from the bucket, between the ʿarāqī (the cross-bars). And it is said that they are called al-Farghānī.

mansions.rising: The rising of al-Fargh al-Muʾakhkhar (the hind Fargh) falls when 14 nights of it have elapsed.

judge.t: The discourse on the mansion of al-Rishāʾ, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (ghayn). When the moon descends into al-Rishāʾ — which is the Belly of the Fish, and it is watery and auspicious — there descends during it into the world a spiritual force of praiseworthy outcome; during it good operations and acts of good outcome are performed; and during it there is conducted /fol. 18r./ the craft of the noble stone and of the magnified, talismanically charged gem. Work upon the spiritual force during it. All operations during it are of praiseworthy outcome. It is suitable for travel, for marriage, for wearing new garments and cutting them out, and for moving from one place to another, and for consorting with sages and chiefs. Whoever is born under it will be blessed, whether male or female. Its suffumigation is black cumin, and God, exalted is He, knows best.

stars.t: As for al-Rishāʾ, it is many small stars in the shape of a fish, called Baṭn al-Ḥūt (the belly of the Fish), and at its navel is a bright star in which the Moon lodges. /fol. 20r./ These, then, are the lunar mansions, which it traverses in every month. Each night the Moon is beside one of them, or near to it; then on the second night it passes on to the one after it, and is [beside] one of them or near to it. Between the rising of the sun and its setting there are 14 of them, and between its setting and its rising 14, and at the time of dawn two of the mansions. All of them rise from the east toward the west; and the time of their rising is to the left of one who is performing the prayer, and the time of their setting on his right, according to the differences of the climes. And the Sun likewise lodges in these mansions.

mansions.rising: The rising of al-Rishāʾ falls on the 4th of Nīsān (April).

season.t: Know that to the season of spring belong al-Sharaṭayn, al-Buṭayn, al-Thurayyā, al-Dabarān, al-Haqʿa, al-Hanʿa, and al-Dhirāʿ; to the season of summer, al-Nathra, al-Ṭarf, al-Jabha, al-Zubra, al-Ṣarfa, al-Simāk, and al-ʿAwwāʾ; to the season of autumn, al-Ghafr, al-Zubānā, al-Iklīl, al-Qalb, al-Shawla, al-Naʿāʾim, and al-Balda; and to the season of winter, Saʿd al-Suʿūd, Saʿd al-Dhābiḥ, Saʿd al-Akhbiya, Saʿd Bulaʿ, the two Farghs — the fore and the hind — and al-Rishāʾ. And to each season belong seven mansions.
